newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RUGBY UNION-SADOURNY INSPIRES FRENCH TOUR WIN.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-SADOURNY INSPIRES FRENCH TOUR WIN.

text.p: France, spurred by two tries from full-back Jean-Luc Sadourny, came from behind to beat ACT President's XV 31-22 on Friday.
Sadourny's impressive finishing gave the Five Nations champions their second win since arriving in Australia for a two-test series against the Wallabies later this month.
But France were forced to dig deep after the home side raced to an early 12-0 lead on tries from veteran fly-half David Knox and flanker Ipolito Fenukitau.
Both sides struggled for fluency in the wet conditions before a small 4,000 crowd at Bruce Stadium.
Wingers Philippe Bernat-Sales and David Venditti and captain Abdel Benazzi also scored tries for France, who led 19-15 at halftime, while centre Christophe Lamaison kicked three conversions.
France suffered a slight injury scare in the second half when Lamaison limped off with a hamstring strain.
Despite the win, assistant coach Pierre Villepreux was unhappy with his side's performance.
"Even when we were down early in the match I thought that when we get some ball we would have no problems. But in the second half we had no possession," Villepreux said.
"We lost too much ball. Also the capacity of ACT to keep the ball meant there were long sequences when we had to defend and defend."

ACT, who reached the Super 12 final last month only to lose to Auckland, were weakened by the absence of leading players including scrum-half George Gregan, winger Joe Roff, centre Pat Howard and flanker Brett Robinson.
They were withdrawn from the match after being selected by Australia coach Greg Smith for the first test in Sydney on June 21. The second test will be in Brisbane one week later.
France thrashed amateur side Victoria in a low-key tour opener on Tuesday.
